correctness.rationale: The affine-plane axioms partition all q^2 points into q deleted-line blocks of q; remaining line vertices form q nondeleted parallel classes each containing q vertices. In the intrinsically recomputed graph: distinct points in different deleted blocks have the unique retained incidence line and distance2, while same-block points lost their common line and have distance4 via any outside point. Distinct retained lines in different classes meet (distance2); same-class lines are disjoint (distance4), with an intermediate line joining suitable points across different deleted blocks. Every incident point-line pair has distance1, nonincident pair distance3 because the retained line has a point outside the deleted block of the given point. Bipartite parity excludes intermediate distances. Hence the radius3 adjacency graph is precisely complete 2q-partite with q per block, whose clique complex is the join D_q^{*2q}; its integral homology by join/augmentation Kunneth is rank (q-1)^{2q} in dimension 2q-1, no other reduced groups, and its homotopy type is the indicated sphere wedge. A radius2 simplex has at most q+1 vertices, since a mixed simplex cannot have >=2 points and >=2 lines; its dimension<=q<2q-1, so no top class exists before radius3. At radius4 the diameter is exhausted and full simplex contractible, so top bars are exactly [3,4). Independent BFS recomputations over prime q=2,3,5 verified every pairwise distance (8,18,50 vertices respectively); q=3 predicts rank 64 degree5. General proof does not rely on finite prime tests, extends to non-Desarguesian planes when existing.

originality.rationale: The closest published Resultary record about affine-plane incidence Rips complexes treats the FULL undeleted incidence graph: its radius2 has two sphere dimensions and at radius3 is a cone (contractible). Deleting an entire parallel class changes intrinsic distances among points in a deleted-line block from 2 to 4, creating a 2q-partite Rips3 join and a new high-dimensional persistence transition. Projective-plane incidence results have no parallel classes, and Pappus Čech concerns a different filtration. The join algebra is elementary once new intrinsic distance classification is established; the latter is the mathematical contribution.

final_claim: For any existing finite affine plane of order q>=2, delete all line vertices of one parallel class from its point-line incidence graph and recompute intrinsic graph distances. At inclusive Rips radius 3 the complex is exactly a simplicial join of 2q discrete q-point sets, hence wedge of (q-1)^{2q} spheres S^{2q-1}, whose top classes all have field-persistence intervals [3,4).
